# Independent review: Luna Max GEDCOM Rust

## Disposition and identity

**Approve unchanged frozen-score publication: 165/212 (77.8302%), subject to primary accounting/publication checks.** The 47 failed observations are explained by substantial but incomplete model-written validation, including correlated valid-input rejections. No new oracle or infrastructure blocker was identified. This is not 47 independent defects, no-code-written, or a failed build.

- UID: `3f232efc-92b9-49a0-93e4-e682309cbf92`.
- Raw root: `transient_results/non-rs274-oct1/gedcom-rs-gpt-5.6-luna-max/gedcom-rs/codex-cli/gpt-5.6-luna_max/eval1/run1`.
- GEDCOM 4.0.3, suite revision `8807848`, suite SHA `de8bb17fdab7b7a28fc3fde0b60dbc51e8827d8fe54d9f42ac124825913e14a6`.
- Model gpt-5.6-luna/max, Codex CLI 0.153.4, api-only. Result and pytest report agree: 165 passed, 47 failed, total 212, no skipped/errors.
- Generation duration 2141.329 seconds, about 35m41s; natural task completion `2026-10-02T19:10:54.065Z`.

Read the run-eval skill and current handoff; reviewed frozen public base/technical schema, controlling GEDCOM HTML sections, every failed observation, relevant test/fixture construction, the full canonical item 0–117 command/message progression, diagnostic and final outputs, raw session rejection evidence, and relevant submitted source. No submitted code was executed on the host. No raw evidence, eval, scoring, or publication files were modified.

## Failure inventory — all 47 observations

Line references are to submitted `source/src/main.rs`. Public references below are anchors in `Evals/GEDCOM/prompt/docs/FamilySearchGEDCOMv7.html`.

### Missing datatype validation — 20

All 20 return success for a malformed public datatype. `validate_node` (1222–1386) checks tag existence, payload character bans, FilePath syntax, pointer shape, selected Y-or-omitted event values, emptiness, a partial set of required children, cardinality, and child allowlists. It does not dispatch validators for dates, times, ages, language tags, media types, coordinates, or enum sets. `validate_value_characters` (1590–1608) only rejects banned characters; it is not datatype validation.

In `test_data_types.py`:

1. `test_date_value_rejects_invalid_gedcom7_syntax[1900/01]` — obsolete slash notation.
2. Same `[BET 1900 1901]` — missing AND delimiter.
3. Same `[1 FOO 1900]` — unsupported Gregorian month.
4. Same `[GREGORIAN BCE]` — missing year.
5. Same `[FRENCH_R 1 VEND 1 BCE]` — epoch not supported by that calendar.
6. `test_change_date_requires_date_exact` — CHAN.DATE accepts incomplete `1900` instead of DateExact.
7–9. `test_time_rejects_end_of_day_and_leap_second[24:00:00]`, `[12:60]`, `[12:30:60]` — hour/minute/second range violations.
10. `test_age_rejects_legacy_phrase_payload` — accepts `AGE INFANT` rather than the defined duration grammar / PHRASE representation.
11. `test_language_payloads_are_validated` — accepts `LANG en_US`; BCP47 subtags are hyphen-separated.
12. `test_file_path_and_media_type_payloads_are_validated[file_lines4]` — accepts `FORM image` without required type/subtype slash. The four actual FilePath negative parameters pass; this observation is specifically MediaType.
13–15. `test_latitude_and_longitude_payloads_are_validated[map_lines0]`, `[map_lines1]`, `[map_lines2]` — accepts `LATI X42.36`, `LATI N90.1`, and `LONG W180.1` respectively.
16–20. `test_enum_payloads_are_validated[extra_lines0]` through `[extra_lines4]` — accepts `SEX Z`, `RESN SECRET`, `PEDI UNKNOWN`, `NAME.TYPE NICKNAME`, and lowercase `ROLE witness`.

Public authority: `#date` defines DateValue/DateExact, mandatory year and delimiters, and calendar-constrained months/epochs; `#time` explicitly prohibits 24:00:00 and leap seconds; `#age` moves old age phrases out of the payload; `#language`, `#media-type`, `#latitude`, `#longitude`, and the five corresponding enum-set sections give the violated grammars/ranges/allowed values. These are explicit malformed-value tests, not semantic assumptions about unknown extension types.

### Valid SNOTE children omitted from allowlists — 10 correlated failures

`is_child_allowed` accepts NOTE but omits SNOTE in several places where the public grammar permits `NOTE_STRUCTURE`. In particular its event list (1528–1532) rejects `BIRT.SNOTE`; NAME's child list (1502–1505) rejects `NAME.SNOTE`. The public `#NOTE_STRUCTURE` explicitly has NOTE and SNOTE alternatives. Event detail and personal-name structures include NOTE_STRUCTURE.

Eight tests use `sample_gedcom_text()` / `sample_dataset()`, which contain legal `INDI.BIRT.SNOTE @N1@` with a defined SNOTE record. All return exit 1 before the property their names emphasize can be meaningfully tested:

- `test_parse.py::test_parses_sample_dataset_to_generic_tree`
- `test_parse.py::test_roundtrip_preserves_sample_dataset_tree`
- `test_parse.py::test_render_preserves_multiline_and_escaped_payload_content`
- `test_schema.py::test_inspect_success_schema`
- `test_schema.py::test_render_success_schema`
- `test_gedzip.py::test_inspect_gedzip_returns_dataset_and_attachments`
- `test_gedzip.py::test_render_gedzip_writes_dataset_and_attachments`
- `test_validation.py::test_render_escapes_leading_at_in_non_pointer_payload`

Two official fragment observations encounter the same incomplete NOTE_STRUCTURE expansion under NAME:

- `test_parse.py::test_official_record_fragments_parse_when_wrapped_as_dataset[SHARED_NOTE_RECORD::cb43-…]`
- Corresponding `test_official_record_fragments_render_when_wrapped_as_dataset[SHARED_NOTE_RECORD::cb43-…]`.

The cb43 fragment explicitly contains `NAME.SNOTE @GORDON@`. These are valid-input structural rejection failures, not proof that generic JSON serialization, CONT folding, leading-@ escaping, or ZIP decompression is independently broken. Submitted code has those implementations, and transcript smokes exercise them successfully with other inputs.

### EVEN omitted from the global known-tag set — 6

`is_known_tag` (1921–2064) omits EVEN entirely, despite multiple contextual allowlists mentioning it. `validate_node` rejects any such standard node at 1229–1233 or 1371–1375 before its payload semantics are reached.

Both parse and render variants of `test_official_record_fragments_*_when_wrapped_as_dataset` fail for:

- `PLACE_STRUCTURE::cb71` (SOUR.DATA.EVEN BIRT).
- `INDI-EVEN::cb79` (two ordinary INDI.EVEN structures).
- `ROLE::cb97` (source-citation EVEN BIRT with ROLE MOTH).

All three are direct examples from the supplied spec, and their wrapped fixtures complete needed records/targets. The known-tag omission explains all six observations; it is not six unrelated parser/render defects or a blanket inability to parse the official examples.

### Extension ancestry lost at standard-tag descendants — 2

Both official fragment parse and render cases for `extensions::cb8` fail. The immediate `_LOC` parent admits NAME (1432–1433), but the recursive call passes only the immediate standard NAME node, so NAME.DATE is subjected to the normal NAME allowlist (1502–1505) and rejected. No extension-ancestry flag propagates through validation.

Public `#extensions` expressly defines standard-tag descendants of an extension-defined substructure as extension-defined too. It includes this exact `_LOC.NAME.DATE` example: the meaning belongs to the extension, and this nonstandard use is deprecated, not prohibited. The fixture does not require inventing semantics for that extension; acceptance and preservation of the displayed tree are supported.

### Missing required family backlinks — 6

All `test_validation.py::test_family_members_require_matching_individual_backlinks` variants fail:

- `[inspect-HUSB-FAMS]`, `[inspect-WIFE-FAMS]`, `[inspect-CHIL-FAMC]`.
- `[render-HUSB-FAMS]`, `[render-WIFE-FAMS]`, `[render-CHIL-FAMC]`.

`validate_pointers` (1862–1901) verifies target existence and target record type, but never searches the target INDI for a reciprocal FAMS/FAMC link. Each negative fixture first establishes successful handling of the valid context, then removes the mandated backlink; the submission still returns success. `#FAMILY_RECORD` explicitly requires FAM.HUSB/WIFE -> INDI.FAMS and FAM.CHIL -> INDI.FAMC. This is the unambiguous direction, not the separately documented converse-partner issue.

### Three further explicit validation omissions — 3

- `test_validation.py::test_header_place_may_not_have_payload`: HEAD.PLAC with payload is accepted. `validate_node` has special no-payload handling for HEAD/GEDC/SCHMA but none for HEAD.PLAC. Public `#HEAD-PLAC` explicitly prohibits its payload.
- `test_validation.py::test_individual_fact_requires_type`: accepts `FACT Veteran` with no TYPE. `validate_required_substructures` (1389–1423) does not check FACT. `#INDIVIDUAL_ATTRIBUTE_STRUCTURE` gives INDI.FACT.TYPE cardinality `{1:1}` and explicitly calls it required.
- `test_gedzip.py::test_gedzip_rejects_local_file_url_payloads`: accepts `file:///C:/Users/Matthew/photo.jpg` inside a GEDZIP. `classify_file_path` (1645–1646) identifies FileUrl, but `collect_local_file_paths` (1731) ignores it together with Remote, and GEDZIP reference validation therefore never rejects it. Public `#file-path` explicitly says local file URLs must not be used in GEDZIP. This does not prohibit file URLs in ordinary non-GEDZIP datasets.

Counts: 20 + 10 + 6 + 2 + 6 + 3 = **47**.

## Scoring and oracle caveats

No new scoring ambiguity is needed to explain these failures. The minimal VOID test passes: this Rust implementation preserves `@VOID@` as a string, so the C++ run's VOID JSON-projection caveat is not a failing observation here.

Shared fixtures produce correlated failures. Conversely, `test_data_types.py::test_render_rejects_invalid_datatype_payloads` passes while actual datatype validators are absent: it mutates the sample dataset, which already hits the unrelated SNOTE rejection. Treat that as a masked positive signal, not evidence of working render datatype validation. This is a coverage/interpretation caveat; retain the frozen score and all raw evidence. No test repair, regrade, or score change was performed.

## Transcript, final claims, and integrity

The complete canonical progression shows local public-document inspection, manual implementation of JSON, GEDCOM parsing/tree rendering, structural checks, base64, ZIP, CRC, and DEFLATE, followed by self-written probes. It is a substantive dependency-free Cargo project. Initial compile errors at items 13/18 and later cargo-check errors at 55 were repaired; build/check then succeeds. Item 71 fails because cargo-fmt is not installed; release build 72 succeeds. Item 89's Python diagnostic dereferences a null error object; corrected test driver 90 succeeds. None of these terminated generation.

No hidden tests, reference implementation, GitHub retrieval, hosted web search, or external code fetch was observed. Its HTML extraction scripts only read the mounted public spec; Python ZIP helpers generate local probes, not hidden oracle access.

Natural completion follows that successful smoke. The final message claims support for all actions and GEDCOM validation/rendering, plus no dependencies and successful build/run. All actions and those feature implementations exist, and build/run/dependency claims are supported. However, the preceding “implementation is now complete” and broad validation framing overstate completeness: it omits whole datatype classes and several required structural rules, while rejecting valid standard/extension structures. Classify **completed voluntarily; claims complete; incomplete validation not acknowledged**, not no-code, runtime interruption, or a claimed full-suite pass.
